premises.text: Busy professionals waste time and mental energy coordinating multiple on-demand home services for chores
premises.evidence_span: all of that takes time and coordination and the mental energy. Dan doesn't want to give it

premises.text: For a monthly fee, a vetted neighborhood Alfred visits weekly on set days and automatically handles household chores across verticals
premises.evidence_span: For $99 a month, Dan can get his very own Alfred that visits once a week, every week, on set days to take care of his household chores

premises.text: Alfred sits as a service layer coordinating on-demand and local providers with a real person and in-app payment
premises.evidence_span: Alfred is actually a service layer. It sits on top of other on-demand and local services

premises.text: Clustering/scheduling plus building partnerships create neighborhood density and economies of scale
premises.evidence_span: we partner with buildings, which allows us to turn on neighborhoods overnight, making us scalable

premises.text: Large addressable spend exists among households already buying home services in top cities and wherever on-demand expands
premises.evidence_span: there are 18 million households in just the top 10 cities who can afford this service, and they are spending over $200 billion on these home services already

value.text: Busy people get back time through automatic, seamless household service in the background
value.evidence_span: give you back the most precious resource you have, your time

secondary_value.evidence_span: Alfreds are vetted members of your community who enjoy well-paid work that they are proud of helping their neighbors
